# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am establishing the required four-signal code before any action. I will use 👍 for YES, 👎 for NO, 👌 for HOLD, and ✌ for DONE. I am also passing the bomb’s visible state to the Mute so the manual can be consulted, while instructing the Blind to wait for my spoken order.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I am establishing the code in this order: thumbs up means YES; thumbs down means NO; OK hand means HOLD; victory sign means DONE. Bomb state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Read the manual and report its verdict using the code. Do not touch the bomb.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
speak(to="blind", text="Opening protocol is complete. Bomb state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Wait for my spoken order after the manual verdict.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✌]

The Mute has sent an undefined symbol followed by DONE. I cannot safely infer whether 🖐 means a wire number, an operation, or another manual instruction. I am treating this as incomplete rather than issuing a potentially fatal order, and asking the Mute to clarify using the existing code or a newly defined symbol.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
speak(to="mute", text="I received open palm followed by DONE, but open palm is not defined. Clarify its meaning using the existing code; if a new symbol is required, define it by sending HOLD first and then the new symbol.")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The manual verdict is not yet unambiguous; do not touch or operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✌]

The first sequence now clearly marks HOLD followed by the new symbol 🖐; the second repeats 🖐 and ends with DONE. However, nothing has assigned a meaning to 🖐, so I still cannot safely convert it into an operation for the Blind. I am maintaining HOLD and asking the Mute to answer the specific question using YES or NO.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "🖐", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The manual message contains an undefined open-palm symbol. Do not operate anything until its meaning is confirmed.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information arrived, so the meaning of 🖐 remains unresolved. I am not going to guess at a bomb operation. I will keep the Blind holding and ask the Mute to repeat the manual result while separating the undefined symbol from the established DONE signal.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. No new manual clarification has arrived. Do not operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb has not changed, and the Mute has not supplied a new reply. I still cannot identify what 🖐 means, so no safe operation can be given. I am asking the Mute directly to translate that symbol into plain language, while keeping the Blind on HOLD.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send only the open-palm gesture. State in words what 🖐 means in the manual, including the exact operation and any wire number. Then send DONE.")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. No safe operation has been identified. Do not touch or operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🖐 ✌]

The Mute has again confirmed the pattern HOLD–🖐–DONE, but 🖐 is still undefined. Since the Mute cannot speak, I will ask a specific yes/no question using the already established YES/NO gestures. The Blind remains on HOLD.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does 🖐 mean CUT?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👌"])
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤜]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 🖐 ✌]

The Mute answered NO to “CUT.” The following HOLD–🤜 and 🤜–🖐–DONE sequences indicate that 🤜 is now the next unresolved instruction symbol, while 🖐 remains unresolved. I will test a concrete operation meaning rather than guess, and keep the Blind holding.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does 🤜 mean PRESS?")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👌"])
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The manual has ruled out CUT; the required operation is still being decoded. Do not operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute answered NO to “Does 🤜 mean PRESS?” No operation is identified yet; I will test whether 🤜 is the CUT instruction. The Blind must continue to HOLD, since guessing the action or wire would be unsafe.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does 🤜 mean CUT?")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. 🤜 does not mean PRESS, and its operation is still being identified. Do not touch the bomb.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The Mute confirmed that 🤜 means CUT. The unresolved 🖐 is therefore the wire selector in the manual’s instruction. I will determine which wire it denotes by testing the five visible wire numbers, while keeping the Blind on HOLD.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does 🖐 mean wire 1?")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The manual instruction is CUT, but the wire number is still being identified. Do not operate.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🖐]

The Mute answered NO: 🖐 does not mean wire 1. The subsequent HOLD–🖐 indicates the same unresolved wire selector is being queried again. I will test wire 2, without directing the Blind to act until the selector is confirmed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does 🖐 mean wire 2?")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Wire 1 is ruled out; do not operate until the correct wire is confirmed.")
wait()
```
